claims.content: Fusion materials must withstand extreme radiation, temperature, and stress.
claims.evidence_span: One remaining challenge is that of materials, which can withstand extreme conditions of radiation, temperature, and stress, with long-term steady properties for the power plant to be economically viable

claims.content: The quaternary alloy formed embrittling Cr- and V-rich precipitates.
claims.evidence_span: However, this quaternary RHEA demonstrated Cr- and V-rich precipitates which could be detrimental to mechanical properties in terms of embrittlement.

claims.content: Iron additions were rejected after producing unwanted intermetallic phases.
claims.evidence_span: the addition of Fe in both low and high elemental concentrations promotes the formation of several undesired intermetallic phases instead of single-phase solid-solution, as well as lowering the melting point of the system. Due to failure of this approach, a quinary HEA was planned

claims.content: A quinary design should improve high-temperature and irradiation resistance.
claims.evidence_span: In this study, a design strategy to further improve the overall response of the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA is introduced and resulted in the development of a quinary RHEA with improved resistance to high-temperature and irradiation environments.

claims.content: Irradiation hardening combines implantation, ballistic-mixing distortion, and grain refinement.
claims.evidence_span: the increase after irradiation is a synergistic combination between Ar implantation, lattice distortion caused by irradiation ballistic mixing, and grain refinement.

claims.content: No dislocation loops appeared after severe dual-beam irradiation.
claims.evidence_span: Dislocation loops were not detected even after 8.5 dpa and at 9.13% He implantation during the dual-beam experiment

claims.content: Hardness rose from 13.25 to 20 GPa through annealing and irradiation.
claims.evidence_span: The average hardness of the unirradiated sample was measured to be 13.25 GPa. After annealing the sample hardness increased to 16.25 GPa, while after irradiation the sample hardness reached a value of 20 GPa.

claims.content: VEC must remain below 4.4 for stable BCC RHEAs.
claims.evidence_span: It has been shown that BCC RHEAs can exhibit high-stability and suitable mechanical properties when the VEC value remains below 4.4

claims.content: Unlike the quaternary alloy, the quinary alloy did not precipitate under irradiation.
claims.evidence_span: This is unlike the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA where irradiation led to uniform and dense Cr-V precipitation

claims.content: Earlier W-based RHEAs combined high melting temperature with better high-temperature strength than Ni superalloys or pure W.
claims.evidence_span: W-based refractory HEAs (RHEAs) have been recently developed in the context of high-temperature applications, showing high melting temperature (above 2873 K) and superior mechanical strength at high temperatures compared to Ni-based superalloys or pure W

claims.content: The preceding W-Ta-Cr-V alloy resisted loops and helium bubbles better than earlier W alloys.
claims.evidence_span: Its response to loop formation under ion irradiation [22] and He implantation [23] is enhanced compared to previously developed W-based alloys, showing no noticeable dislocation loop formation and smaller He bubbles with no radiation-induced segregation at grain boundaries upon heavy ion irradiation and He implantation, respectively.

claims.content: Dual-beam irradiation reverses annealing-driven grain growth and refines the grains.
claims.evidence_span: After He implantation, the grain size further increased to 36.3 ± 1.8 nm. However, during the dual-beam irradiation, grain refinement occurred, and the average grain size dropped to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm

claims.content: Hf segregation to grain boundaries accounts for annealing hardening.
claims.evidence_span: The increase in hardness after annealing was ~3 GPa and this can be directly attributed to Hf segregation to grain boundaries

claims.content: Inverse Kirkendall transport or ballistic mixing depletes Hf from irradiated grain boundaries.
claims.evidence_span: The EDX demonstrated depletion of Hf from grain boundaries during irradiation which can be attributed to the Inverse Kirkendall effect (IKE) [36] and/or ballistic mixing during irradiation [37]

claims.content: Irradiation homogenized the elements and produced no precipitates.
claims.evidence_span: The irradiated part showed homogenization of the elements and no precipitation.

claims.content: The rough helium energy landscape favors rapid trapping at stable bubble nuclei.
claims.evidence_span: This rough energy landscape implies that He has a higher tendency to quickly find a fairly stable site that can act as a bubble nuclei

claims.content: Near the Hall-Petch crossover, small grain refinement can cause a large hardness increase.
claims.evidence_span: This change is higher when the grain size is very small and approaches the edge of the transition from the Hall-Petch to the Inverse Hall-Petch effect

claims.content: CALPHAD predicts a single BCC phase over a wide temperature range.
claims.evidence_span: which are predicted by CALPHAD to form a single-phase BCC structure over a wide temperature range

claims.content: Irradiation cavities reached a saturation regime after initial formation.
claims.evidence_span: No increasing trends in cavity volume, density, or change in volume occur after that, and saturation is evident for these dpa/He percentage ranges.
